content.title: About
content.content: Rice dressing is a seasoning made from rice vinegar, soy sauce, sugar and aromatic additives. It has a light sweet‑sour note, a subtle rice aroma and is used in Asian cuisine to dress salads, rolls, and to marinate fish and vegetables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rice dressing originated in Japan in the early 20th century as a milder alternative to traditional soy sauce.
There are several variants: sweet (with honey or sugar) and more acidic (with higher rice‑vinegar content).
It is commonly used in sushi rolls, giving the dishes a characteristic shine and aroma.
Unlike plain vinegar, rice dressing contains a small amount of amino acids formed during rice fermentation.
In some countries it is called “rice‑vinegar sauce,” although its composition differs from pure vinegar.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Rice dressing contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Fermentation preserves polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The mild acidity stimulates gastric juice production, aiding digestion.

items.title: Reduced sodium compared to soy sauce
items.content: Some versions have lower salt content, which can be beneficial for blood‑pressure control.

items.title: Moderate glycemic impact
items.content: Added sugar is usually modest, so the glycemic response remains moderate.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Because many recipes include soy sauce, people with soy allergy should avoid it.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweet varieties may contain noticeable sugar, which is undesirable for diabetics or weight‑loss plans.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Although lower than soy sauce, the dressing still contains sodium; hypertensive individuals should monitor portions.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some commercial products add food preservatives; choose additive‑free versions if you have sensitivities.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use rice dressing as a salad dressing, a marinade for fish, seafood or chicken, and to drizzle over sushi rolls and rice dishes. It can be mixed with ginger, garlic or sesame oil for a more complex flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dressing in a tightly sealed bottle in the refrigerator after opening. At room temperature it may keep up to 6 months, but flavor and aroma last longer when chilled. Discard if you notice color changes, off‑smell or sediment.
